question: Should OpenClaw add first-party per-agent backup/restore/clone semantics to the core backup CLI now, and if so what credential/session portability contract should it enforce?
rationale: The feature would rewrite config entries and persisted agent state while copying sensitive credentials and transcripts, and the current code has no established restore contract to extend mechanically.

options.title: Sponsor core design
options.body: Define a first-party per-agent archive/restore contract in core, including credential exclusion/copy rules, transcript snapshot policy, rollback, and archive compatibility tests.

options.title: Fold into broader backup work
options.body: Keep this open but block implementation until the encrypted snapshot and general restore direction settles a single archive format and restore safety model.

options.title: Reject core clone for now
options.body: Document private workspace backup plus manual agent creation as the supported path and leave full per-agent clone to future plugin/API design.

recommendation.title: Sponsor core design
recommendation.body: Define a first-party per-agent archive/restore contract in core, including credential exclusion/copy rules, transcript snapshot policy, rollback, and archive compatibility tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent database-first state, auth storage, and backup documentation work makes this the best available routing owner for the product/security decision.
